feedback.problem:
Find, in ascending powers of $b,$ the **first three terms** in the binomial expansion of ${(1-5b)}^{10}.$

$(1-5b)^{10}=$
{{field-1}}$\,+\,⋯$
feedback.worked_solution:
The first three terms of the binomial expansion for $(1+x)^{n}$ are given by

$$
(1+x)^{n}=1+nx+\frac{n(n-1)}{2!}{x}^{2}+⋯.
$$

By substituting $x=-5b$ and $n=10$ into the above formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{(1-5b)}^{10} & =1+10\cdot (-5b)+\frac{10(10-1)}{2!}\cdot (-5b)^{2}+⋯ \\  & =1-50b+\frac{10\cdot 9}{2}\cdot 25{b}^{2}+⋯ \\  & =1-50b+45\cdot 25{b}^{2}+⋯ \\  & =1-50b+1\,125{b}^{2}+⋯\end{aligned}
$$
